findings.body:
**The header describes a push protocol that the code does not implement. Update the header.**

`src/selfhost/promote-gate.ts` Lines 84-90 say that one `ls-remote` re-reads the queue right before the push. They also say "only main is sent" when the queue still equals the tip, and that the queue refspec "rides along" only when the queue moved.

The code at Lines 1263-1282 behaves differently:
- It runs no `ls-remote`.
- It always sends three leased refspecs: `main`, `cq/promoted` and `merge-queue`. The `merge-queue` refspec is leased at `tip`.
- The inline comment at Lines 1263-1272 and the tests at `test/selfhost/promote-gate.test.ts` Lines 1562-1590 and 1676-1686 confirm the "luna round 4" three-ref design.

The header omits the `cq/promoted` marker update entirely. Operators read this header as the authoritative trust description of the gate, so the mismatch misleads audits of D-K.6. The same stale claim appears in other places:
- `test/selfhost/promote-gate.test.ts` Lines 16-18 say "the push sends ONLY main".
- The real-git test name at Line 2339 says "with only the main refspec".
- Line 2356 says "The queue is NEVER written by the gate". In fact the gate always pushes the queue refspec, and that push is a no-op update leased at the tip.

<details>
<summary>📝 Proposed header fix</summary>

```diff
-//      `push --atomic` of tip
-//      onto main — leased on the (main, tip) read at step 1, never a plain
-//      force. One `ls-remote` right before the push re-reads the queue on
-//      the push's own transport: still the tip (the normal case) → only
-//      main is sent (D-K.6 by construction); moved → the merge-queue
-//      refspec rides along as a pure lease whose failure refuses the whole
-//      push, so a break-glass rewind is never re-promoted.
+//      `push --atomic` of three leased refspecs, never a plain force:
+//      subject:main (leased at the step-1 main), subject:cq/promoted (the
+//      replay marker, leased at its pre-push read), and tip:merge-queue
+//      (always leased at the run-start tip — a no-op when unchanged; any
+//      queue movement rejects the whole push, so a break-glass rewind is
+//      never re-promoted).
```
</details>
findings.title: The header describes a push protocol that the code does not implement. Update the header.
